chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shummun, from Abdillah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Mis'mam ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who made a vow but did not specify a thing, so he said: 'If he wishes, he prays two rak'ahs; and if he wishes, he fasts for one day; and if he wishes, he gives charity with one loaf of bread.'

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What to do if you make a vow but forget to specify what you vowed to do?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for a general vow (nadhr mutlaq) by offering three accessible options, reflecting the Shia principle of facilitating religious obligations. The choice between prayer, fasting, or charity highlights the flexibility in fulfilling vows, with the minimal charity option emphasizing ease for the common believer. This ruling is often cited in fiqh discussions regarding the fulfillment of unspecified vows, prioritizing intention and feasibility.
